requirement: The notice itemises the categories of personal data collected, in plain language.
A specific purpose is stated for the data collected; generic 'business purposes' is only Partial.
The notice is clear, plain-language and understandable on its own.
Processing is on a stated lawful basis (consent or a legitimate use).
Collection is limited to data necessary for the specified purpose (purpose/data limitation).
If legitimate uses are relied upon, they fall within the Act's Section 7 categories.
A commitment to keep personal data accurate, complete and up to date.
A retention period, or an 'erase when the purpose ends' commitment, is stated.
Reasonable security safeguards (encryption, access control) are disclosed.
A commitment to notify affected users and the Board of a personal-data breach.
Withdrawal of consent is offered and is as easy as giving it, with a route stated.
Consent is a clear affirmative action, unbundled, not pre-ticked or implied.
The Consent Manager route is acknowledged where relevant.
Users can review consent given / records of consent are maintained.
Verifiable parental consent for under-18s, and no tracking, behavioural monitoring or targeted ads to children.
The right to access a summary of personal data being processed is disclosed.
The right to correction of personal data is disclosed.
The right to erasure of personal data is disclosed.
A readily available grievance-redressal route is disclosed.
The right to nominate is disclosed.
A reachable grievance officer or business contact for data queries is published.
A Data Protection Officer is appointed and published (Significant Data Fiduciary).
Processors engaged only under a valid contract.
Third parties / recipients of data sharing are disclosed.
Sub-processor oversight is addressed.
Security obligations flow down to processors.
Transfers of personal data outside India are disclosed.
Compliance with any restricted-country notification is addressed.
Data storage location is disclosed.
A Data Protection Impact Assessment is undertaken (Significant Data Fiduciary).
Privacy by design and periodic audit are addressed.
Data-minimisation measures by design are addressed.
A published privacy policy exists and is reachable.
A cookie policy / tracker disclosure is published.
Terms of service are published.
Notice is available in an accessible form (and Indian languages where relevant).
Registered office / entity contact details are published.
The site serves over HTTPS (encryption in transit).
Encryption at rest is disclosed.
Access controls and logging are disclosed.
An internal data-protection policy / governance is in place.
Staff are trained on data protection.
Records of processing activities are maintained.
An incident-response plan exists.
Vendor / third-party risk management is addressed.
Significant-Data-Fiduciary obligations / Board reporting are addressed where applicable.
